subject: Food Science
title: Rancidity
description: A micro-lesson that makes Rancidity usable.

hook.text: Open a bag of stale chips and the smell hits you. That's rancid fat—oxidized oils producing foul aldehydes.

buildup.text: Oxidative rancidity happens when unsaturated fats react with oxygen. Light, heat, and metals speed it up.

discovery.text: Polyunsaturated oils go rancid fastest because more double bonds means more sites for oxygen to attack.

twist.text: That's why fish oil supplements smell terrible when old—fish oil is extremely polyunsaturated.

climax.text: Antioxidants like vitamin E slow rancidity. Dark bottles protect olive oil from light-driven oxidation.

punchline.text: Fat plus oxygen plus time equals rancid. Protect your oils.

quiz.question: Why do polyunsaturated oils go rancid faster?
options: More double bonds provide more sites for oxygen to attack
